original_question: Given an n x n square subdivided into n^2 unit squares in the usual way, call a line intersecting a unit square if the line and the unit square share a common point that is an interior point of the unit square. Determine the minimum number of lines needed so that every unit square is intersected. In particular, decide whether this minimum equals n - 1 for every n >= 3.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 9, “Lines crossing all squares of the board.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it has the n x n square subdivided into n^2 unit squares, uses the same interior-point notion of when a line intersects a unit square, asks for the minimum number of lines meeting all unit squares, and preserves the paper’s highlighted subquestion asking whether the minimum is n - 1 for every n >= 3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
missing_details: For a fully stand-alone formulation, the quantifier on n should be explicit: the paper starts with n as a positive integer. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The ambient setting should be made explicit: these are ordinary straight lines in the Euclidean plane, and the square is an n-by-n square in that plane. The paper leaves this geometric ambient space implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

It helps to say explicitly that every one of the n^2 unit squares must be intersected by at least one line; this is the intended covering condition in Problem 9. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The paper does not add any extra restrictions on the lines (for example, no slope, position, lattice-point, or boundary-passing conditions), so a stand-alone rewrite should avoid introducing any such restrictions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
refined_question: Let n be a positive integer, and let an n x n square in R^2 be subdivided in the usual way into n^2 unit squares. Say that a line intersects a unit square if the line and the square have a common point lying in the interior of that unit square. What is the minimum number of lines in R^2 needed so that every unit square is intersected by at least one of the lines? In particular, is this minimum equal to n - 1 for every n >= 3? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Problem 9 in Section 6, not a broader neighboring problem. Section 6 is devoted to “Lines crossing all squares of the board,” and Problem 9 asks for the minimal number of lines intersecting all unit squares of an n-by-n board, followed by the specific question whether that minimum equals n - 1 for n >= 3. The surrounding context adds only the definition of what it means for a line to intersect a unit square; there is no nearby theorem, proposition, or explicitly stated equivalent reformulation to substitute for Problem 9. So the paper-faithful rewrite is essentially the same question with the ambient Euclidean setting and quantifier on n made explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
